o: Direct channel opening at all doses

pharm-neuro:neuromap.q: A 40-year-old woman with refractory status epilepticus is placed in a pentobarbital coma in the ICU. At the GABA-A receptor, this drug acts by:
pharm-neuro:neuromap.e: Barbiturates prolong channel opening (and directly open it at high doses); benzodiazepines increase opening frequency.

pharm-neuro:aed-focal.e: Also teratogenic (fetal hydantoin), SJS, CYP induction.

pharm-neuro:aed-focal.q: A 30-year-old woman of Han Chinese descent with focal impaired-awareness seizures starts a new antiseizure drug. Three weeks later she has fever, painful target lesions and oral and conjunctival erosions with < 10% epidermal detachment. Genotyping shows HLA-B*15:02. Which drug was most likely started?
pharm-neuro:aed-focal.e: HLA-B*15:02 strongly predicts carbamazepine-induced Stevens–Johnson syndrome, so screening is advised in Asian patients before starting it.

pharm-neuro:aed-absence.q: Which drug can worsen absence seizures?

A 7-year-old girl has brief staring spells many times a day, each lasting about 10 seconds without postictal confusion; one is provoked by hyperventilation. EEG shows 3-Hz spike-and-wave discharges. The drug of choice acts by:
pharm-neuro:aed-absence.e: Childhood absence epilepsy is treated with ethosuximide, which blocks thalamic T-type Ca²⁺ channels; Na⁺ channel blockers like carbamazepine can worsen absences.

pharm-neuro:aed-broad.q: Valproate is contraindicated in pregnancy because of:
Lamotrigine must be titrated slowly to avoid:

A 25-year-old woman with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy (morning jerks, generalized tonic-clonic seizures) is well controlled on valproate but plans pregnancy next year. Which drug is the most appropriate replacement?
pharm-neuro:aed-broad.e: Valproate is highly teratogenic (neural tube defects); levetiracetam is broad-spectrum and safer in pregnancy. Carbamazepine and phenytoin can worsen myoclonic seizures.

pharm-neuro:barb-bzd.e: Also status epilepticus. Risk of dependence and additive CNS depression with alcohol.

pharm-neuro:barb-bzd.q: A 48-year-old man with heavy daily alcohol use is admitted for hip surgery. Forty-eight hours later he has tremor, sweating, HR 118/min, BP 165/100 mm Hg and visual hallucinations. Most appropriate drug and its action?
pharm-neuro:barb-bzd.e: Alcohol withdrawal is treated with a benzodiazepine, which substitutes for alcohol's GABA-A effect; haloperidol lowers the seizure threshold and does not treat withdrawal.

pharm-neuro:insomnia.q: A 68-year-old woman takes a nightly hypnotic for sleep-onset insomnia. Her husband finds her cooking in the kitchen at 3 AM, and she has no memory of it the next morning. Which drug most likely caused this?
pharm-neuro:insomnia.e: Complex sleep behaviors (sleepwalking, sleep-driving) are a boxed warning for the BZ₁-selective 'Z-drugs'; ramelteon (melatonin agonist) does not cause them.

pharm-neuro:triptans.e: Vasoconstriction and inhibition of trigeminal activation.

pharm-neuro:triptans.q: A 45-year-old woman has recurrent unilateral throbbing headaches with nausea and photophobia lasting 12 hours. She also has variant (Prinzmetal) angina with documented coronary vasospasm. Which abortive drug is contraindicated?
pharm-neuro:triptans.e: Triptans are 5-HT₁B/1D agonists that constrict coronary arteries, so they are avoided in vasospastic angina and CAD; NSAIDs and antiemetics are safe options.

pharm-neuro:pd.q: A 68-year-old man with Parkinson disease has taken levodopa–carbidopa for 6 years. His tremor and rigidity now return about 3 hours after each dose, before the next one is due. Which added drug most directly prolongs each dose's effect?
pharm-neuro:pd.e: Wearing-off is managed with a COMT inhibitor (entacapone), which blocks peripheral levodopa breakdown; benztropine helps tremor but does not extend levodopa action.

pharm-neuro:neurodeg.q: A 74-year-old woman has 3 years of progressive memory loss and now gets lost in her neighborhood. MMSE is 20/30 and MRI shows hippocampal atrophy. After starting a drug she develops bradycardia and diarrhea. The drug acts by:
pharm-neuro:neurodeg.e: Alzheimer disease is treated with donepezil; ↑ ACh causes cholinergic effects (bradycardia, diarrhea). Memantine (NMDA antagonist) does not cause these.

pharm-neuro:localanes.e: They bind from inside the axon. Small myelinated fibers are blocked first.

o: Speeds onset by raising tissue pH
pharm-neuro:localanes.e: Vasoconstriction ↓ systemic absorption. Avoid in digits and penis classically.

pharm-neuro:localanes.q: A 32-year-old man has a fluctuant, erythematous thigh abscess. After lidocaine is infiltrated into the inflamed tissue, incision is still very painful. Why is the local anesthetic less effective here?
o: Acidic pH keeps drug in charged form
pharm-neuro:localanes.e: Local anesthetics are weak bases that must be uncharged to cross the nerve membrane; acidic infected tissue keeps them ionized. Amides are metabolized in the liver, not by pus.

pharm-neuro:genanes.q: Inhaled anesthetic potency is inversely related to:

pharm-neuro:genanes.e: Ryanodine receptor defect triggered by volatile anesthetics and succinylcholine.

pharm-neuro:genanes.q: A 19-year-old man undergoing appendectomy under sevoflurane and succinylcholine develops masseter rigidity, rising end-tidal CO₂, tachycardia and a temperature of 40.5 °C. The drug of choice acts by:
o: Blocking nicotinic receptors at the NMJ
Blocking RyR1 Ca²⁺ release from the SR
pharm-neuro:genanes.e: Malignant hyperthermia (RyR1 defect) is treated with dantrolene, which blocks Ca²⁺ release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum; nondepolarizing blockers do not stop the intracellular Ca²⁺ leak.

pharm-neuro:nmb.e: Depolarizing; dangerous in burns, crush injury, denervation.

pharm-neuro:nmb.q: A 35-year-old man with 40% total body surface area burns sustained 10 days ago needs rapid-sequence intubation for débridement. Succinylcholine is avoided because it may cause cardiac arrest through:
pharm-neuro:nmb.e: Burns, crush injury and denervation upregulate extrajunctional ACh receptors, so depolarization releases large amounts of K⁺; MH requires an inherited RyR1 mutation.

o: GABA-B receptors in the spinal cord
α₂ receptors in the spinal cord

pharm-neuro:relax.q: A 30-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis has painful spasticity and flexor spasms of both legs that interfere with walking. Which drug is most appropriate?
pharm-neuro:relax.e: Baclofen (GABA-B agonist in the spinal cord) treats spasticity from MS and spinal cord injury; cyclobenzaprine is for acute musculoskeletal spasm, not upper motor neuron spasticity.

pharm-neuro:opioids.q: Which opioid effect does NOT develop tolerance?

pharm-neuro:opioids.e: ↓ Ca²⁺ influx presynaptically, ↑ K⁺ efflux postsynaptically.

pharm-neuro:opioids.q: A 58-year-old man with metastatic lung cancer has taken escalating oral morphine for 6 months. His pain is controlled and early sedation resolved, but he has hard stools every 5 days despite osmotic and stimulant laxatives. Best drug and its action?
pharm-neuro:opioids.e: Constipation shows no tolerance; a peripherally restricted μ antagonist relieves it without reversing analgesia. Loperamide is a μ agonist and would worsen it.

pharm-neuro:mixed.q: Tramadol lowers seizure threshold and can cause:
pharm-neuro:mixed.e: Weak μ agonist plus SNRI action.
Can precipitate withdrawal in opioid-dependent patients.

pharm-neuro:mixed.q: A 45-year-old man taking sertraline for depression is prescribed a new analgesic for back pain. Two days later he is agitated and diaphoretic with temperature 38.9 °C, inducible ankle clonus and hyperreflexia. Which property of the analgesic explains this?
pharm-neuro:mixed.e: Tramadol is a weak μ agonist that also inhibits 5-HT and NE reuptake, so with an SSRI it can cause serotonin syndrome; D₂ antagonism relates to neuroleptic malignant syndrome instead.

pharm-neuro:glaucoma.e: β-blocker acting on the ciliary epithelium. Systemic absorption may worsen asthma.

pharm-neuro:glaucoma.q: A 64-year-old man with moderate persistent asthma is found to have open-angle glaucoma (IOP 28 mm Hg, cupped optic discs). Which eye drop should be avoided?
pharm-neuro:glaucoma.e: Topical nonselective β-blockers are absorbed systemically and can trigger bronchospasm; prostaglandin analogs, α₂ agonists and carbonic anhydrase inhibitors are alternatives.

pharm-neuro:status.q: Fosphenytoin is preferred over phenytoin IV because:
o: It does not cause gingival hyperplasia
It has no CYP450 drug interactions
pharm-neuro:status.e: Prodrug; purple glove syndrome with phenytoin.

pharm-neuro:status.q: A 28-year-old man with epilepsy has a generalized tonic-clonic seizure lasting 10 minutes. He received two doses of IV lorazepam and is still seizing; airway and IV access are secured. Most appropriate next drug?
pharm-neuro:status.e: After benzodiazepines fail, a second-line IV agent (fosphenytoin, valproate or levetiracetam) is loaded; oral drugs act too slowly and haloperidol lowers the seizure threshold.

title.th: เคสใหญ่: มือสั่นเดินช้า

boss.case: A 67-year-old man has a 1-year history of resting tremor of the right hand, slowness of movement and a shuffling gait. Examination shows cogwheel rigidity and reduced arm swing. He is cognitively intact.

o: Is converted to dopamine in the brain
qs.e: ↑ CNS levodopa and ↓ peripheral side effects.

qs.q: A dopamine agonist such as pramipexole may cause:
Which drug worsens his symptoms and should be avoided?

qs.e: Antimuscarinic. Avoid in elderly due to confusion.

title.th: ปวดหัวข้างเดียวตุบๆ

stem.th: หญิง 26 ปี ปวดหัวข้างเดียวตุบๆ มีคลื่นไส้ กลัวแสง เป็นเดือนละ 6 ครั้ง
stem.en: A 26-year-old woman has throbbing unilateral headaches with nausea and photophobia, 6 times a month.

steps.q: Acute treatment for a moderate–severe attack:
Sumatriptan should be avoided if she has:
steps.e: Coronary vasospasm; also avoid in Prinzmetal angina.
Amitriptyline and anti-CGRP antibodies are alternatives. Daily triptans cause medication-overuse headache.

info.th: ต้องการยาป้องกัน

steps.q: A topiramate adverse effect to counsel about:
steps.e: Also weight loss and paresthesias; may ↓ contraceptive efficacy at high doses.

info.th: เธอใช้ยาคุมกำเนิด และเลือก topiramate
info.en: She uses oral contraceptives and chooses topiramate
